heading.en: Earned but not received, received but not earned

hook.en: A tenant pays three months' rent in advance; a bank credits interest only after the year ends. Profit must show *income* earned, not just cash received.

title.en: On the board: Accrued income and income received in advance

say.en: Income earned but not received is accrued income. Income received for next year is received in advance.
Accrued income is added to the income and is an asset. Advance income is deducted and is a liability.
Hari & Co.: 10 percent on 50,000 is 5,000 due; 3,000 received, so 2,000 has accrued.
Rent received 18,000 includes 4,500 for next year: only 13,500 is this year's income.

caption.en: A tenant pays rent to us every quarter. The income of the year is always four quarters: quarters earned but not received are accrued income; quarters received for next year are income received in advance.
caption.kn: ಬಾಡಿಗೆದಾರ ಪ್ರತಿ ತ್ರೈಮಾಸಿಕ ಬಾಡಿಗೆ ಕೊಡುತ್ತಾನೆ. ವರ್ಷದ ಆದಾಯ ಯಾವಾಗಲೂ ನಾಲ್ಕು ತ್ರೈಮಾಸಿಕ: ಗಳಿಸಿ ಪಡೆಯದದ್ದು ಬರಬೇಕಾದ ಆದಾಯ; ಮುಂದಿನ ವರ್ಷಕ್ಕೆ ಪಡೆದದ್ದು ಮುಂಗಡ ಆದಾಯ.

problem.en: Hari & Co. holds 10% investments of ₹50,000 for the whole year; interest received ₹3,000. Rent received ₹18,000 includes ₹4,500 for the next year. Find the amounts for the final accounts.

steps.en: Interest in P&L = 3,000 + 2,000 = ₹5,000; accrued interest ₹2,000 is a current asset.
Rent in P&L = 18,000 − 4,500 = ₹13,500; rent received in advance ₹4,500 is a current liability.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Hari & Co. holds 10% investments of ₹50,000 for the whole year; interest received ₹3,000. Rent received ₹18,000 includes ₹4,500 for the next year. Find the amounts for the final accounts.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Hari & Co. holds 10 percent investments of 50,000 rupees for the whole year; interest received 3,000 rupees. Rent received 18,000 rupees includes 4,500 rupees for the next year. Find the amounts for the final accounts.
Interest due equals 10 percent times 50,000 equals 5,000; received 3,000; accrued interest equals 2,000 rupees.
Interest in P&L equals 3,000 plus 2,000 equals 5,000 rupees; accrued interest 2,000 rupees is a current asset.
Rent in P&L equals 18,000 minus 4,500 equals 13,500 rupees; rent received in advance 4,500 rupees is a current liability.
So the answer is Interest 5,000 rupees (asset 2,000 rupees); rent 13,500 rupees (liability 4,500 rupees).
